raw.what_makes_this_different: Narma's distinction lies in its "Enterprise Agentic Brain" which observes work patterns and creates a "Work Graph" to identify specific opportunities for AI intervention and agent deployment, rather than developing new foundation models. This enables "Continuous AI lift" by ensuring AI is applied where it provides the most value, directly addressing challenges with AI ROI and deployment at scale.
raw.thesis: Narma proposes an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" for AI-first companies to facilitate the adoption and scaling of AI automation. The core innovation lies in its three-layered architecture: an "Observe" layer with desktop sensors capturing work patterns; an "Intelligence Layer" or "Brain" that identifies employee intent, business value, and workflow "drift"; and a final layer that continuously builds AI agents. It leverages existing foundation models, focusing on a "Work Graph" to identify inefficiencies and opportunities for AI intervention. This venture directly addresses the challenges enterprises face in measuring AI ROI, pinpointing AI savings, and managing system/human resource drift. Narma aims to provide a single system that observes work, determines AI actions, and continuously deploys AI agents, ensuring "Continuous AI lift." The founder envisions this as a growth startup, given the stated goal of enabling AI at scale for AI-first companies. The venture is currently at the idea stage, with the founder describing the concept and architecture without mentioning any built product or users. The venture seeks to complement existing AI solutions by providing the intelligence layer for deploying and managing AI agents at scale within an enterprise, rather than replacing fundamental AI models or human workers. It precedes the widespread and efficient deployment of AI automation by providing the critical observation and intelligence layer.

raw.product_description: Narma is a three-layered "Enterprise Agentic Brain" designed for AI-first companies. The first layer "Observes" work patterns through lightweight desktop sensors, capturing application usage, activity sequences, and time allocation. The second, "Intelligence Layer" or "Brain," detects employee intent, the business value of tasks, and "drift" in workflows. The system leverages existing foundation models and focuses on building a "Work Graph" to identify where AI can intercept work. The vision is a single system that observes work, decides AI actions, and continuously auto-builds agents for "Continuous AI lift."
